key_insight: Band alignment at 2D/3D perovskite interfaces is highly sensitive to surface termination and chemical composition, making interface engineering a key lever for passivation and performance.
engineering_relevance: Accurate control of 2D/3D interface chemistry can help stabilize perovskite solar cells while preserving charge extraction and minimizing energy barriers.
method: Atomistic first-principles simulations with hybrid functionals
Computed work function, electron affinity, and band offsets across cleavages/interfaces
Compared multiple 2D/3D perovskite compositions and terminations
evidence_signal: The abstract reports preliminary hybrid-functional results showing work functions, macroscopic potential slopes, and band offsets that vary substantially with termination and ionic substitution.
watch_item: Results are preliminary and interface-specific, so conclusions may shift with additional structures, defects, and experimental validation.
paper_title: Material chemical composition impacts on the band alignments: preliminary results on the 3D/2D perovskite interfaces
